evidence: M-O s.v. football: rugby, American football
terms.comment: Classically harpastum is a small hard ball and the rough game played with it, in which the players snatched the ball from one another (Mart. 4.19.6, 7.67.4). “Play rugby” is harpastō lūdere (Traupman).
Where it must be told apart from American football; Morgan–Owens also offers harpastum Rugbiēnse, after the school.

phrases.english: or if you snatch the dusty harpastum with your hand

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 49, checked against the searchable text of the book on 11 November 2026.
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. football: rugby, American football …; football: rugby: rugby.
